主要内容: Health insurance costs are set to rise in 2020, with large employers predicting the total cost of covering health insurance for workers and their families will reach an average of $15,375, a 5% increase from 2019. Employees are expected to cover about $4,500 in expenses, including out-of-pocket spending. Deductibles now account for more than half of workers' out-of-pocket spending, up from 26% in 2008. Employers are reintroducing preferred provider organization (PPO) plans, which allow access to any in-network provider without a referral. Virtual care and accountable care organizations are also expected to play a larger role in 2020. Brian Marcotte, CEO of the business group, emphasized that the rising costs are a direct result of the growing demand for health care services. Marcotte's comments highlight the ongoing challenges faced by the insurance industry in balancing affordability and coverage. The statement was made in an article published on September 26, 2019, by CNBC, which is noted as a trusted source for business news.
